anchor: PC&PNDT Act implementation and regulation of diagnostic technologies
argumentsAgainst: A regulatory framework can become ineffective if inspections, enforcement and follow-up on violations are inconsistent across States/UTs.
Digital processes may improve monitoring but can also create privacy, access and implementation concerns if safeguards and capacity are inadequate.
argumentsFor: Regular inspection of registered facilities and prompt action on violations can strengthen deterrence.
Capacity building of Appropriate Authorities, engagement with medical professionals and inter-State sharing of good practices can address implementation gaps.
Responsible use of technology can support healthcare and social inclusion without enabling sex selection or gender discrimination.
background: The Central Supervisory Board (CSB) reviewed implementation of the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994, at its 32nd meeting on 19 November 2026.
The meeting addressed gender-biased sex selection, misuse of diagnostic technologies, digital processes, capacity building and coordination among States/UTs.
The source record does not provide the statutory composition, powers or detailed provisions of the Act; these should not be inferred from this note.
indiaImplications: Effective implementation can support gender equality and the social value of the girl child.
Centre–State coordination is necessary because implementation activities, inspections and enforcement require action by States/UTs and local authorities.
Technology governance must balance healthcare innovation with safeguards against sex selection and gender discrimination.
Improved implementation may complement awareness efforts such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, while legal enforcement alone cannot substitute for education and social attitude change.

officialFacts.text: The 32nd meeting of the Central Supervisory Board reviewed implementation of the PC&PNDT Act, 1994.
The SRS 2024 Report records the national sex ratio at birth at 918.
The Union Health Minister called for strengthened State-level action, an effective monitoring framework and responsible use of technology.
The Central Supervisory Board deliberated on strengthening PC&PNDT Act implementation through digital processes, capacity building and inter-State collaboration.

example.heading: Illustration: coordinated monitoring
example.text: Suppose a State identifies repeated compliance concerns across registered facilities. A coordinated response could combine regular inspections, trained Appropriate Authorities, medical-professional engagement and sharing of good practices with other States. This is a hypothetical illustration, not a reported event.

pocketRead.excerpt: The CSB’s review connects inspections, trained authorities, digital processes and inter-State cooperation to preventing misuse of diagnostic technologies and gender discrimination.

question.answer: A balanced approach would combine regular inspections and prompt follow-up with trained Appropriate Authorities, medical-professional engagement, inter-State sharing of good practices, responsible digital monitoring and sustained community awareness. This addresses both enforcement gaps and the social attitudes that sustain gender discrimination.
question.prompt: How should India strengthen PC&PNDT implementation without treating technology or enforcement alone as a complete solution?

sections.heading: Implementation, not prohibition alone
paragraphs: The Central Supervisory Board reviewed the PC&PNDT Act’s implementation on 19 November 2026. The mechanism identified in the release is cooperative enforcement: States/UTs inspect registered facilities, follow up on violations, build institutional capacity and share practices.

sections.heading: Technology with safeguards
paragraphs: Digital processes can help integrate monitoring, but the release’s central limitation is clear: technology must not facilitate sex selection or gender discrimination. Regulation therefore requires both technical capacity and sustained engagement with medical professionals and communities.

sourceTitle: 32nd Meeting of Central Supervisory Board Reviews Implementation of PC&PNDT Act, 1994
staticDefinition: The PC&PNDT framework is presented in the source as the legal and institutional framework whose implementation is reviewed by the Central Supervisory Board to address gender-biased sex selection and misuse of diagnostic technologies. The source does not establish the Act’s detailed statutory prohibitions or institution
use: Use as a GS1 society and GS2 health-governance example of how gender discrimination, medical regulation, Centre–State coordination and responsible technology governance intersect.

advisory_notes: The proposed codes GS1.5, GS2.6 and GS2.7 are plausible, but the GS1 society linkage is secondary; the strongest fit is GS2 health, governance and Centre–State relations.
The explanation that implementation requires State and local action is sound, but detailed statutory institutional roles are not established by the supplied release alone.
The phrase “State inspections” is supported by the release’s call for regular inspections, while “risk-based” inspections are a reasonable recommendation rather than a reported measure.
“Prompt action” should preferably be written as prompt follow-up on violations, matching the release’s wording and avoiding an implied completed enforcement outcome.
The claim that legal enforcement alone cannot substitute for education and social-attitude change is sound analysis, not a direct finding of the release.
The counter-position about displacement of malpractice and the privacy and access concerns around digitisation are analytical extensions and should remain clearly framed as risks.
The pocketRead headline, deck, paragraphs and applied-question answer accurately present the release’s implementation themes; the example is correctly labelled hypothetical.
The SRS figure is better specified as 918 female births per 1,000 male births during 2022–24, rather than simply “national sex ratio at birth at 918.”

wayForward: Ensure regular, risk-based inspection of registered facilities and prompt, procedurally fair follow-up on violations.
Strengthen the capacity of Appropriate Authorities and maintain continuous engagement with medical professionals.
Use interoperable digital monitoring with privacy, accountability and non-discrimination safeguards.
Institutionalise inter-State sharing of enforcement practices and targeted interventions.
whyInNews: On 19 November 2026, the Central Supervisory Board reviewed implementation of the PC&PNDT Act, 1994 and discussed gender-biased sex selection, misuse of diagnostic technologies, digital processes, capacity building and inter-State collaboration. The meeting also recorded the SRS 2024 national sex ratio at birth as 918.
